newsitem.title: USA: Iowa community to try another bid for gaming boat.
newsitem.headline: Iowa community to try another bid for gaming boat.

text.p: The central Iowa community of Osceola plans to ask the state gaming commission in the fall to approve another plan for a floating casino on West Lake, administrator Brad Wright said Friday.
It will be the third time Osceola asks the Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission to license a casino on the Clarke County lake about 40 miles south of Des Moines, Wright said.
The commission has twice rejected bids by Alton, Illinois-based Argosy Gaming Co and Osceola has chosen a different operator for its next attempt, Wright said.
City and county officials signed a letter of intent with Southern Iowa Gaming Co on May 27 for an estimated $40 million boat and land access plan, Wright said.
The casino would generate a projected $2 million annually in total tax revenues for the city, county and schools, Wright added.
The new gaming company is 100 percent owned by William M. Grace, who also owns a casino in St. Joseph, Missouri.
The Grace casino would be located on a different part of West Lake than the proposed Argosy boat with a new site for on-land access, Wright said.
After the last commission hearing in April on the Argosy bid, it became apparent board members were not rejecting the community, only Argosy, Wright said.
"We got a clear message that we had to find another operator for the boat," Wright said.
The gaming commission has required new applications to be submitted only in December, but plans to rescind that requirement, Wright said.

The capacity and land-based facilities would be substantially the same as the Argosy bid, but the plan also includes a request for new access ramps onto I-35 that would create a direct route to the new development and current facilities, Wright said.
